set.title: Views & nets of 3D objects · Unit Test

questions.question: Ava unrolls the paper label and lids of a cylindrical oatmeal container so the whole container lies flat. Which set of flat shapes is the net of a cylinder?
questions.explain: A cylinder unrolls into 2 circles (the top lid and the bottom) plus 1 rectangle for the curved side. The usual trap is drawing only 1 circle because the bottom of the container is forgotten.

questions.question: Noah lines up identical cubes on his desk to make a flat slab that is 3 cubes wide (left to right), 2 cubes deep (front to back) and 1 cube high. What does the FRONT view of his slab look like?
questions.explain: From the front you only see width and height, so the 2 cubes of depth hide behind each other and you see 1 row of 3 squares. The common trap is drawing the 3-by-2 rectangle, which is the top view, not the front view.

questions.question: Mia is drawing a labelled net for a rectangular gift box that is 8 cm long, 5 cm wide and 3 cm high. On her net, what are the dimensions of the face that sits flat on the table (the base)?
questions.explain: The base lies flat, so it uses the two measurements that run along the table — length and width — giving 8 cm by 5 cm. The common trap is pulling in the height (3 cm), which belongs to the front and side faces instead.

questions.question: Sofia builds a model out of centimetre cubes for art class. Looking straight down from above, she sees one row of 3 squares. Looking from the front, she sees a row of 3 squares with 1 extra square stacked on top of the left-hand one. What is the fewest number of cubes her model can contain?
questions.explain: The top view says the model is only 1 cube deep with 3 positions, and the front view says those positions are 2, 1 and 1 cubes high, so 2 + 1 + 1 = 4 cubes. The common trap is adding the squares in the two views (3 + 4 = 7) instead of using the views together.

questions.question: Liam builds a cube staircase that is only 1 cube deep. The bottom layer is 3 cubes in a row; a second layer of 2 cubes sits on the left end; a third layer of 1 cube sits on top of the far-left column. What does the RIGHT SIDE view of the staircase look like?
options: A staircase shape made of 6 squares
A row of 3 squares side by side
questions.explain: From the right side you see depth and height: the model is 1 cube deep and 3 cubes tall at its tallest, so the side view is 1 column of 3 squares. The common trap is redrawing the staircase, which is what you see from the front, not the side.

questions.question: Rowan is drawing a full-size net for a cylindrical hot-chocolate tin with a diameter of 10 cm and a height of 12 cm. Using π ≈ 3.14, what size should the rectangle (the curved side) be?
questions.explain: The long edge of the rectangle wraps right around the circle, so it equals the circumference: 3.14 × 10 = 31.4 cm, and the other edge is the height, 12 cm. The common trap is using the radius (3.14 × 5 = 15.7 cm) or the circle's area instead of its circumference.

questions.question: For a store window in Kelowna, Jayden stacks identical cube-shaped boxes. From above the display looks like a filled 2-by-2 square. From the front it looks like a filled 2-by-2 square, and from the right side it also looks like a filled 2-by-2 square. What is the fewest number of boxes Jayden could have used?
questions.explain: The top view forces 4 boxes on the floor, and the second layer only needs 2 boxes placed on a diagonal so that every column and every row still reaches 2 high — that is 4 + 2 = 6. The common trap is assuming the views mean a completely solid 2-by-2-by-2 block of 8, but views show the outside only and hidden gaps are allowed.

questions.question: For a recycling project, Priya cuts 6 identical cardboard squares and tapes them edge to edge, hoping to fold each arrangement into a closed cube. Which arrangement will NOT fold into a cube?
options: A row of 4 squares, with 1 square joined above the second square and 1 square joined below the third square
6 squares taped into a 2-by-3 rectangle (2 rows of 3)
A row of 3 squares, with a second row of 3 squares joined underneath but shifted across so the rows overlap in only one column
A column of 4 squares, with 1 square joined to the left of the second square and 1 square joined to the right of the third square
questions.explain: A cube net needs a strip of 4 squares to wrap around as a band plus one square for the top and one for the bottom; in the 2-by-3 rectangle no such band exists, so two faces overlap and two holes are left open. The common trap is thinking any 6 joined squares make a cube — only 11 of the arrangements actually fold.
